authorization: User approved implementation and verification in an independent temporary Orca source copy.

repair.owner: Orca runtime PTY record; no Companion readiness bypass
repair.activity: Bounded per-PTY scanner and three input-mode values distinguish complete repeated bracketed-paste, modifyOtherKeys and absolute kitty settings. Other output counts as activity and forgets the previous mode evidence.
repair.parser: Reuse and extend the existing scanner with non-CSI observations, pending state, generic ESC/CSI and C1 control strings. Oversized unfinished escapes retain an unrecognized bounded prefix; OSC may end in BEL, other control strings require ST.
repair.rawOutput: onPtyData keeps raw byte forwarding, output sequence and both PTY/leaf lastOutputAt clocks unchanged.
repair.strongReadiness: Only existing strong quiet-ready body rules consume the activity clock. The 3000ms threshold, trusted-grid composer and working/menu/overlay vetoes remain.
repair.weakReadiness: Weak title and foreground-process lanes retain the raw clock. An untrusted or absent screen cannot use protocol reassertions to relax foreground readiness.
repair.recheckTimers: Keep existing raw-clock scheduling. These timers re-evaluate evidence when they fire and do not decide readiness themselves; switching to an already quiet activity clock would cause unnecessary 50ms rechecks while a screen or working veto still holds.
repair.pending: Unfinished parsing closes readiness lanes while preserving blocked/working verdicts.
repair.lifecycle: Same-incarnation reattach preserves activity. Incarnation replacement, dropped-output gap and confirmed PTY exit clear activity/parser state. No separate persistent clock or wire DTO is added.

verification.toolchain: Existing Companion node_modules symlink: Vitest 5.0.1 and Vite 8.3.0. A temporary config avoids unavailable Electron tsconfig; no dependency installation.
